findings.title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height variant
findings.body:
`OptimizedImage.downsize` is defined twice: `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the width/height signature no longer exists.

Every existing caller using `downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)` now fails:
- With five arguments it raises `ArgumentError`.
- With four arguments, `max_height` (an Integer) is bound to `opts`, and `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` raises a `TypeError`.

This breaks existing downsizing (e.g. avatar and thumbnail code paths). Give the new method a distinct name, or have a single method that accepts both forms.

findings.title: Animated GIF downsizing passes a percentage to gifsicle, which it cannot use
findings.body:
When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is on and the file is a `.gif`, `optimize` routes to `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. `--resize-fit` expects WxH dimensions, not a percentage.

As a result:
- gifsicle exits non-zero.
- `downsize` returns false, and the result is ignored.
- The loop burns all 5 attempts doing nothing.
- The oversized GIF is passed on unchanged and then rejected.

Animated GIFs, often the largest images, are never reduced.

findings.title: In-place rewrite of tempfile path may leave the open Tempfile handle stale
findings.body:
The loop rewrites the file at `tempfile.path` in place. `convert` writes there, and `ImageOptim#optimize_image!` replaces the file, typically by writing a new file and renaming it over the path. The open `Tempfile` IO can still refer to the original inode.

If so:
- `tempfile.size` keeps reporting the original size, so the loop always runs the full 5 iterations of expensive conversions.
- `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, ..., tempfile.size)` may read the original, unreduced content and size.

Also, the return value of `downsize` is ignored, so a failed conversion keeps looping. Re-open the file or use `File.size(tempfile.path)`, and stop when `downsize` returns false.

findings.title: Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types, ignoring site settings
findings.body:
`validateUploadedFile` now uses a fixed 10MB limit instead of `max_<type>_size_kb`. That limit is only meant to let oversized images through for server-side downsizing, but it also applies to attachments.

Consequences:
- Attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` pass client validation, upload fully, and are only rejected by the server.
- Sites configured with limits above 10MB can no longer upload files the server would accept.

The same hardcoding at line 246 makes the 413 error message report 10MB regardless of the real limit. Keep the setting-based limit for attachments, and only relax it for images.

findings.title: URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB regardless of upload type or settings
findings.body:
API URL uploads are now capped at a fixed 10MB instead of following site settings. Two effects:
- Admins who raised `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB can no longer upload such files by URL.
- Attachments up to 10MB are downloaded even when the configured attachment limit is far smaller, wasting bandwidth before the inevitable rejection.

findings.title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing path or the `downsize` signature change
findings.body: The PR adds the server-side downsize loop and changes the `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures without adding any specs. A spec covering the old `downsize(from, to, w, h)` callers would have caught the method-redefinition breakage. A spec for oversized image uploads, including GIFs, would have caught the gifsicle issue.
